rule: Never run Conductor from source (python launch.py). Always use the installed exe at %APPDATA%/Redis Operator/Conductor.exe
reason: Source and exe use different SQLite databases. Running from source creates/modifies a different conductor.db than the one the exe uses, causing workers to go missing or duplicate.

rule: The AppData DB is the source of truth: C:/Users/jarms/AppData/Roaming/Redis Operator/conductor.db
reason: The exe reads from AppData. The repo has its own conductor.db which is stale. All MCP interactions go through the exe which uses the AppData DB.

rule: Do not recreate the Cowork VM Monitor worker — it was deleted intentionally
reason: Worker #4 caused a fork bomb that exhausted system resources. The VM runs fine without monitoring.

rule: Conductor's auto-launch logic must use both process detection (tasklist) and file locking. Never trust port-check alone.
reason: The exe takes several seconds to bind port 5000 after launching. A port-check alone races during that window and can spawn multiple Conductor instances. Multiple instances = multiple schedulers firing the same cron = cascading subprocess explosions.

rule: All subprocess-spawning scripts (SMTP, HTTP, etc.) must have explicit timeouts
reason: Without a timeout, a hung network call keeps the subprocess alive forever. When a scheduler fires repeatedly, dead subprocesses stack up and exhaust resources.
